summary:
A visitor to Córdoba operates under Argentina's national legal framework, and nothing in the available sources records a provincial rule departing from it. Law 26.743, promulgated on 24 May 2012, allows a change of legal gender without surgery, without hormone treatment and without judicial approval, while anti-discrimination protection runs through a combination of national and provincial statutes.

Emergency Decree 62/2025, issued in February 2025, amends the Gender Identity Law to bar under-18s from gender-affirming surgery and comprehensive hormonal treatment; Decree 61/2025 governs the placement of transgender people in the prison system. Both bind every province, including Córdoba. FALGBT announced legal action against the decrees, and constitutional experts described them as unlawful.

Violence data bear directly on this province. Agencia Presentes reported on 19 March 2026 that Argentina's national hate-crime observatory recorded 227 hate crimes against LGBT+ people in 2025, a 62% increase amounting to one every 38 hours. Security-force institutional violence rose to 64 cases from 17 in 2024, and 32% of incidents occurred in police stations or prisons; in 43% of cases the perpetrators were unknown to the victims. Between 18 and 26 November 2025, police in Salta, Córdoba and Buenos Aires provinces intervened in the deaths of three LGBT+ people over eight days, with Córdoba's forces explicitly named in that documented pattern.
tangentialFactors:
The national hate-crime figures are raw counts for the whole country and are not adjusted for population, so they cannot be read as a per-province ranking. The observatory's 2025 total of 227 incidents is a national aggregate; the only province-specific datum in the sources is the November 2025 sequence in which Córdoba police were named alongside Salta and Buenos Aires.

Argentina's national anti-discrimination agency was abolished and shut down in February 2024 as a public-spending measure, removing a federal complaint channel that a visitor might otherwise have expected to exist.
localsOnly:
Residents of Córdoba, including trans residents, remain covered by Law 26.743's provisions on legal gender change and access to sex reassignment surgery and hormone therapy through public and private health plans, subject to the February 2025 under-18 restrictions imposed by Decree 62/2025.

Decree 61/2025 governs how transgender people are housed in the prison system; the sources do not set out its operative terms.

Provincial police forces in Córdoba were named in the documented November 2025 pattern of interventions in the deaths of LGBT+ people, and 32% of nationally recorded incidents took place in stations or prisons, settings where provincial forces hold custody.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources do not state whether Córdoba province has its own anti-discrimination statute or hate-crime provision, or how its courts have handled gender-identity cases; that layer is unresolved here.

The operative terms of Decree 61/2025 on prison placement are not provided in the inventory and remain unsourced.

No per-province breakdown of the 227 nationally recorded 2025 hate crimes is available, so Córdoba's share of that total cannot be stated.
